properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 11/03/2025 to PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC in Sheffield Township, Warren county. 102.22(b)1 - SITE STABILIZATION – TEMPORARY STABILIZATION – Permitee failed to temporarily stabilize the site to protect it from accelerated erosion and sedimentation where cessation of earth disturbance activities exceeded 4 days.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/03/2025
Violation Code: 102.22(b)1 - SITE STABILIZATION – TEMPORARY STABILIZATION – Permitee failed to temporarily stabilize the site to protect it from accelerated erosion and sedimentation where cessation of earth disturbance activities exceeded 4 days.
Violation ID: 8254676
Permit API: 123-49141
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sheffield Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/03/2025
Comments: This recently drilled conventional well was shut in. Drill cuttings have been directed into a lined pit. The drilling permit and E and S Plan were posted at the entrance of the location. The access road and well site location have been stoned, however, due to the recent drilling traffic during wet conditions the road material has lost its durability. The road leading to the well was reshaped after the rig moved out, however, clean stone should be considered to provide a durable road surface for the upcoming completion and production of this well. Due to the lack of energy dissipators and culverts, the road ditch is experiencing high flow, and is therefore, showing signs of accelerated erosion. The ditch will need to be reshaped, graded, and temporarily stabilized. Additional culverts, as called for in the E and S Plan, will need to be installed in order for the ditch to function properly. Only 2 out of the 4 culverts called for in the E and S Plan have been installed. The 2 culverts installed have not been installed in accordance with the E and S Plan. The lone culvert on the slope of the access road leading to the well site is poorly positioned with a majority of stormwater flow bypassing the inlet and continuing to flow down the ditch rather than out-letting through the culvert. According to the E and S Plan, stone rip-rap should be placed below the outlets to dissipate the outfall. Infiltration berms should be installed beyond the outlet of the culverts. The outlets are directing stormwater at un-stabilized fill material from the construction of the road. None of the outlets have stone rip-rap or an infiltration berm to dissipate the outfall of stormwater. These concerns should be addressed as outlined in the E and S Plan.A majority of the seed and mulch on the road banks and surrounding the well location have washed away with only sparse vegetation established. These areas will need to be re-seeded and mulched in order to eventually achieve permanent stabilization, prevent accelerated erosion from occurring, and meet the requirements of Chapter 102. The recent drilling traffic has also caused significant rutting on FR 413A. This road is expected to be properly shaped with a functional ditch or other measures to manage stormwater. Clean stone should be considered in certain areas to improve the durability given the additional development related traffic that will be using this road. Also, installing tail ditches or other measures to improve the drainage of the road should be considered to allow for the road to remain in compliance throughout the remaining development of this well and well #1. A follow up inspection will be conducted to ensure the above concerns have been addressed properly and in a timely manner. Due to the risk of pollution via accelerated erosion and sedimentation it is highly recommended to address these concerns prior to the next rain event.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 1/06/2021 to EQT PROD CO in Forward Twp, Allegheny county. 78A57(A)___ - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator discharged brine and other fluids on or into the ground or into the waters of this Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT PROD CO
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/06/2021
Violation Code: 78A57(A)___ - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator discharged brine and other fluids on or into the ground or into the waters of this Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 903930
Permit API: 003-22234
Unconventional: Yes
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Forward Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/06/2021
Comments: This inspection is taking place in response to a spill reported by the operator on 12/27/2020 as well as a follow up to a previously reported spill from 8/15/2020 which has been reported as remediated. The operator reported that the spill occurred at approximately 9:30 PM when a check valve washed out. The operator reported approximately 1 barrel of Production Fluid was discharged to the ground. When asked via phone on 12/28/2020, Mr. Hardy reported that the operator would remediate the spill in accordance with Act 2. The following is observed: The Act 9 Sign is present, the ERP, PPC, and associated SDS are in the mailbox adjacent (Photo 1). The operator has removed material between GPUs 2H and 3H (Photo 2) thereby constructing a sump approximately a foot and a half deep and nearly the length of the GPU (Photo 11). Background readings taken in the area were between 70 uS and 300 uS (Photo 12 & 13). Readings taken in the vicinity of standing water in the sump were between 2,000 uS and 13,500 uS. Readings of 2,000 uS were detected between the skids of GPU 3H (Photo 16 & 17). GPU 3H is attached to GPU 16H, on the other side of this structure between another piece of Production Equipment was another smaller "sump" (Photo 6). Background in this area was around 500 uS (Photo 7). Readings taken around this sump were detected at 7,000 uS to 13,000 uS (Photo 5 & 8). GPUs 3H and 16H do not appear to have adequate secondary containment. Per the CO&A entered into on 12/17/2020, these are noted as ICS. The Department requests information on how the operator is going to remediate the impacted material in accordance with 91.33(B) and submit it before 1/11/21. Additionally, the Department requests more information on how the discharge reached the other side of 16H and how the operator intends to remediate any impacted material below the GPUs. The Department requests information on how the amount spilled was quantified. The Department also requests a copy of the waste manifest once it is available. In reference to the 8/15/2020 spill, it appears that sump has been back filled (Photo 19). The Department requests documentation including photographs of the remediation effort prior to filling in the excavated area and including conductivity readings adjacent to and under the GPU. Based on this inspection, violations are being issued for the discharge to the ground associated with GPU 3H. Violations associated with the spill that occurred on 8/15/2020 and referenced in IR 3096843 will remain outstanding. Pending the operators response, further violations may be issued.

Comments: On 3/14/2024, Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) representative John Rogers conducted an incident inspection at the Watkins Unit 820 well site located in Chatham Twp, Tioga Co. This was in response to spill notification CID# 378902 of a release of produced water and oil-based mud to a 40'x40' section of the pad surface. The release was reported as coming from the annulus of a plugged well on site.It was 55 degrees and clear when I arrived on site. I met up with DEP inspectors, Lester Tayler and Scotty Brown. Prior to my arrival, Lester received the following information from Seneca's Rick Dake: Rick discovered the release on 3/14/2024 at 1500 hours. Fluid was on the pad surface and was spitting out and leaking from the 13x9 annulus of the Watkins 25H plugged OG well. Rick explained the release as being caused by rainwater flowing across the pad and into the 25H well cellar. The rainwater flowed down the annulus and pushed the lighter weight oil-based mud to surface. During the inspection, I did witness a crew using two excavators and a small front-end loader to scrape the area north and east of the 25H well cellar of loose gravel. The gravel they were scraping was wet and dark colored. The pad surface was void of water puddles and was a lighter color. This excavation area extended approximately 40' from the south side of the well cellar to the north with production equipment limiting the extent of the excavation. Dark staining marked the pad surface as the release spread on an eastward path to the riprap lined channel below the cut slope on the east side of the pad. I did witness dark brownish black blobs of liquid floating on water within the riprap channel. 3-inch boom absorbents had been placed within the riprap lined channel at the north and south extents of the visible contamination. The distance between the north and south booms was approximately 50 feet.Miller Environmental Group was on site providing cleanup activities to the site. Miller's project manager, Ernie Ginoble, said that he had responded to the site at 1500 on 3/13/2024 and provided initial response actions while assessing the scene. The cleanup crew mobilized equipment to the site on 3/14/2024 at 0630. He said that they were scraping down approximately 6 inches to a cemented layer of the pad. They were placing the excavated material into plastic-lined rolloff dumpsters that were being staged on secondary containment on the southwest corner of the pad. Prior to my leaving, they had filled three dumpsters with two more available at the site. A vac truck was on site sucking up free liquids from the pad surface and from the 25H well cellar. A vac box arrived at the site during the inspection to allow for additional volume.There is a house and a farm north of the property and houses south of the property. I did not witness any residential property to the east or to the west. The area is pasture type grasses. There is a stream across the road to the west.This spill constitutes violations of these three regulations; 78a 57(a), SWMA 301, and CSL 402(b). The DEP recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation in accordance with 78a 66(c).During a phone conversation after the inspection, Seneca's Jeff Passerrello did report that Seneca will pursue Act 2 for the release.I departed the site at 1350 hours.

Violation ID: 931498

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/24/2021
Comments: Inspection in response to a discharge of gas and crude oil from this well reported to the Department at 0250. The County HazMat Team and Department ERT were called to the incident and reported the incident as venting of crude oil and gas from a pressure relief valve on top of a tank. During the response, it was reported that the pump jack eventually stopped operating and the discharge of crude oil tapered off and essentially stopped. The valve continued to vent natural gas. The County HazMat Team strung caution tape around the well site, laid down pig matting where crude oil had sprayed and absorbent booms around the puddles of crude oil (Photos 1-8). Accompanying me during inspection is OGI Jon Shub (DEP) and Josh Boarts, the well tender for the operator. Boarts began clean up efforts by filling buckets with the oil that surrounded the well head and dumping it into the brine tank on site (Photo 9). Boarts then laid down pig matting around all affected areas and then absorb-it on the areas around the pump jack and well head (Photos 20-23). The spill was generally contained within the area of which the yellow tape is surrounding the site. The area around the well is flat aside from the depression around the pump jack that allowed the crude oil to pool around it. The closest Water of the Commonwealth is Deer Creek which is approximately 300 feet East of the well, but does not appear to be in danger of contamination due to the flat parking lot in which the well sits. According to the owner of the property, who has a video feed of the well, the discharge began at approximately 22:04 on 9/23. Oil had discharged up until the early morning when the HazMat team was on site. Josh Boarts estimated the spill to be around half a barrel while on site. The exact cause of why the pressure valve was released is unknown to the operator at this time, but the well tender Josh Boarts did say the valve is supposed to release at 250 lbs of pressure. Boarts was provided with the Department spill policy and program clarification memo. Boarts plans to gather visibly impacted material into large barrels before properly removing them off site.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/09/2022 to BULL RUN RESOURCES LLC in Keating Twp, McKean county. 78.64(d)1 - CONTAINMENT AROUND OIL TANKS - For tank capacity of at least 660 gallons or tanks with a combined capacity of at least 1,320 gallons, the owner or operator drained tank containment facilities which caused a harmful discharge or resulted in a sheen.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BULL RUN RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/09/2022
Violation Code: 78.64(d)1 - CONTAINMENT AROUND OIL TANKS - For tank capacity of at least 660 gallons or tanks with a combined capacity of at least 1,320 gallons, the owner or operator drained tank containment facilities which caused a harmful discharge or resulted in a sheen.
Violation ID: 964818
Permit API: 083-57144
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Keating Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/09/2022
Comments: This conventional well has recently been produced with a pump jack, there was no activity on this location or throughout the Cole Creek lease during this inspection.A tank battery consisting of a 210 bbl steel stock tank and a poly brine/production water tank is located approximately 150 feet to the south of this well. These tanks are contained by an earthen dyking which has been lined and partially filled with gravel. Holes have formed throughout the exposed portion of the liner along the upper edge of the containment wall.Fluid was trickling out of the containment drain pipe into the roadside ditch upon my arrival at the tank battery. There was no supervision of this discharge and the drain is not equipped with a valve. A shower drain cover was fitted onto the inlet of this drain. The specific conductivity (SPC) of the fluid inside of the containment exceeded the upper threshold of my field meter (20,000 uS/cm). Pooled fluid in the ditch was also greater than 20,000 uS/cm. Deer tracks are abundant around the pooled fluid in the roadside ditch. This evidence suggests that the fluid being discharged from the containment drain is production water/brine. An SAC 941 sample was collected from the fluid discharging from the drain. The fluid in the roadside ditch flowed through a cross culvert and into a forested area. Poor road conditions have allowed stormwater to run off of the road surface above this culvert, which allowed the released fluid to migrate further into the forested area. Elevated SPC of pooled water and soil (along with stressed vegetation) was observed in various pathways across the forest floor west of the tank battery for approximately 200 feet downslope of the tank battery. The most downward extent of the apparent impacted soil (near a property boundary/corner marker) is approaching a channel (currently dry) that develops into an unnamed tributary of Cole Creek.After this inspection, I spoke with Justin Hansen of Bull Run to discuss the aforementioned issues along with concerns regarding the roads, site identification and actions necessary to consider this well site restored. In order to consider utilizing the containment drain, the fluid that is currently pooled inside of the containment will need to be removed along with the saturated gravel. Prior to any future discharges from the drain, the water should be tested as per the regulations to ensure it meets the criteria to be released under sufficient supervision.Future inspections will be conducted to review the current state of affairs with Bull Run personnel and evaluate remediation measures outside of the containment as they take place.

Comments: On July 22, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Chabal 2 well site in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3985188 where violations issued from IR 3965337 were left outstanding. During the time of IR 3985188, remedial excavation was completed and the impacted soil was stockpiled onsite awaiting disposal. The impacted soil stockpiles were covered and appeared to be adequately protected to mitigate risk of the impact being spread by stormwater.The following was observed:The well head is equipped with a well tag and appears to be free of fluid leaks at the time of inspection (see photo 2). However, leaking gas was audible from the top of the well head (see photo 3). The operator's information is posted on the separator (see photo 4). The brine tank that was present at the time of the Department's previous surface inspection has been replaced. The newly-installed brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection, with no elevated soil conductivity detected underneath the brine tank valve (see photos 7-9 and 18). It appears that the stained material noted underneath the brine tank during the time of IR 3967072 has been removed (see photo 10). It appears that the impacted soil stockpiles have been removed from site, as they were not present onsite during this inspection.The slope that was impacted by the 4/24/2025 release has been backfilled, mulched, and seeded. It has established some vegetative coverage, although it is inconsistent at the time of inspection (see photos 11, 13, and 14). An erosion rill has developed at the top of this slope (see photo 12). Compost Filter Sock (CFS) and straw bales are installed at the bottom of the formerly impacted slope (see photo 15). No elevated soil conductivity was detected in this location or at the approximate downslope edge of the formerly impacted area (see photos 16-18).The Department notified the operator of the erosion rill observed during this inspection via voicemail, and recommended that it is repaired and measures are taken to protect it from heavy stormwater events while it establishes vegetative coverage.Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that remedial work has been completed and the site awaits completion of re-stabilization. However, violations issued from IR 3965337 shall remain outstanding, as an NOI to Remediate and/or Final Report has not yet been submitted to the Department's ECB for review.Additional violations may be forthcoming pending reassessment and reevaluation of the erosion rill in a future follow-up inspection conducted by the Department.

The well was reportedly plugged on 2/27/2025, therefore the site shall be restored no later than 11/27/2025. Present during the inspection was operator representative Joe Miller.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection the Department was unable to locate a restoration plan onsite. Therefore, the Department was unable to compare the well site to the restoration plan. The Department recommended to Mr. Miller that the site restoration plan be present at the well site until the Post Plugging Well Site Restoration Report is submitted and approved. Mr. Miller stated he would ensure a copy is brought to the well site and remain there until the Post Plugging Well Site Restoration Report is submitted and approved.Upon inspection of the access road, it appeared to have achieved 70% uniform and adequate vegetative coverage. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed at the time of the inspection. Upon inspection of the former well site, the Department observed an above ground monument for the reportedly plugged well. No other production equipment was observed on site. There were no observed leaks at the surface in the area surrounding the well monument. The well site did appear to have achieved 70% uniform and adequate vegetative coverage. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed at the time of the inspection.The Department informed Mr. Miller that the site is to be restored 9 months after plugging of the well,and that the well was reportedly plugged on 2/27/2025, therefore the site shall be restored no later than 11/27/2025, and that the Post Plugging Well Site Restoration Report is due 60 days after restoration. The Department then recommended Mr. Miller submit the Post Plugging Well Site Restoration Report if the site is restored in accordance with the restoration plan.Based on today's inspection, violations associated with no erosion and sedimentation controls installed are being closed as the site has achieved 70% uniform and adequate vegetative coverage. The violation regarding no E and S/Restoration Plan onsite is outstanding.

A second location (Photo's 4-7) is actively discharging sediment laden water into WOTC. The water appears to be pooling at a low point on the access road, spilling into a ditch which is conveying through a culvert pipe underneath the access road into a stream heading in the direction of Trib 37653 of Sewickley Creek. A straw bale barrier at this location does not appear to have been installed correctly (See Standard Detail 4-13 in the E&S Manual 363-2134-008, pg. 90). The bales do not appear to have been staked, trenched, or back fill applied. This appears to have allowed sediment laden stormwater to go around the bales and enter WOTC. The Department recommends that the operator immediately address this deficiency in order to prevent any further impacts to WOTC. The well appears plugged with a monument present with the API number affixed. There is no machinery present on the site. The site does not appear to have been temporarily stabilized and no down slope E&S controls are present. There does not appear to be an E&S Plan on site. The Department recommends that the operator take immediate steps to temporarily stabilize the site to prevent the potential for accelerated erosion or sedimentation. The Department recommends that the operator have E&S Plans prepared by a person trained and experienced in E&S Control methods and techniques applicable to the size and scope of the project and that those plans be on site during all phases of the earth disturbance activity. The Department also recommends that the operator installs downslope controls to prevent accelerated erosion and sedimentation from occurring at the site. An operator representative was spoken to via phone about the conditions on site. Mr. Wagner stated that no E&S Plans had been developed for this project and due to the weather conditions, no efforts were made to stabilize the site against accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Based on this inspection violations are being issued to the operator. The Department requests a timeline and action plan for abating the discharge and possible discharges identified in this inspection. Further violations may be issued based on responses received from the operator.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-06-29 to Bull Run Resources Llc in Wetmore Twp, McKean county. 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Bull Run Resources Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-06-29
Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 887751
Permit API: 083-54017
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Wetmore Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-06-29
Comments: The operator contacted Brian Ayers to report multiple spills at the Collins Pine 22 well site the morning of 6/29/2020. This inspection was performed as a complaint inspection to CID #350759. The operator was intending to perform an injection test on this well for a proposed injection well permit. They had a 500 barrel laydown tank on location that was filled with brine over the course of several days prior to the test. The operator noted on arriving at the site 6/29 that the site was wet, and then was able to see that the tank was actively leaking brine. They were able to contact a vac truck operator who sent trucks to empty the tank. A mini excavator was used to dig a small trench on the north side of the site. In the interim, the operator hooked a hose from the tank to drain into the well in order to reduce the level of the tank. The packer in the well failed, which allowed oil to be displaced and flow out the backside of the packer string and onto the ground. The operator noticed the discharge and immediately shut the well in and ceased flowing water. They had a mini excavator on site and dug another interceptor trench in the access road to cut off oil from flowing further down gradient toward Route 6. 1-2 barrels of oil was estimated to have been released from this well. At the time of this inspection, the operator had determined that 3" of water had drained from the full tank prior to discovery of the leak, which occurred at approximately 10 am. Further leaking occurred during the time between discovery and the emptying of the tank at approximately 2 PM. The total loss of brine is estimated to be between 5 and 10 barrels. Various areas surrounding the tank were tested with a soil EC meter, which read between 15 mS and >20 mS. Oil was all contained within the trench or puddles on the location, with no threat of further contamination. The operator intends to have a rolloff container on site this evening and begin to scrape up the contaminated soil on site, starting with the area contaminated with crude oil. A vac truck will be on site should extra encountered.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/03/2025 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. 91.33(A) - INCIDENTS CAUSING OR THREATENING POLLUTION - Failure to notify the Department of an accident or other activity or incident, a toxic substance or another substance which would endanger downstream users of the waters, result in pollution or create a danger of pollution of the waters of this Commonwealth, or would damage property.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/03/2025
Violation Code: 91.33(A) - INCIDENTS CAUSING OR THREATENING POLLUTION - Failure to notify the Department of an accident or other activity or incident, a toxic substance or another substance which would endanger downstream users of the waters, result in pollution or create a danger of pollution of the waters of this Commonwealth, or would damage property.
Violation ID: 8227910
Permit API: 123-47902
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/03/2025
Comments: The R H Stevenson Lease 4 conventional well is the nearest conventional well in proximity to the tank battery on the R H Stevenson lease. The tank battery is situated within earthen containment and consists of an upper level containing two stock tanks, and a lower level containing two polyurethane tanks. The stock tanks are plumbed into PVC piping that extends along the rear of the upper level of the earthen containment until terminating into the first of the two polyurethane tanks in the lower level. The first of the two polyurethane tanks in the lower level is also equipped with additional PVC piping apparently for the purpose of either removing or depositing fluids into the tank in the lower level of containment. At the time of this inspection, standing pools of fluid present in the upper level of the containment were found to have specific conductance measuring 5,980 microSiemens per centimeter (uS/cm). It was observed that straw had been laid down beneath the PVC piping in the upper level of containment. Where the straw cover ends, fluid was found to be actively flowing from the upper level of containment to the lower level. No fluid was observed to be flowing through the PVC piping connecting the stock tanks to the polyurethane tank during the time of this inspection. Neither polyurethane stock tank was found to have a noticeable volume of fluids contained within them at the time of this inspection. Some accumulation of fluids and crude oil could be observed around the base of the polyurethane tanks in the lower level of the containment at the time of this inspection. The flow of fluids from the upper level to the lower level of containment was not found to be accumulating nor increasing the accumulated volume of fluids and crude oil present at the bottom of the lower level of the containment at the time of this inspection.Approximately 40 feet south of the lower level tank battery containment area, crude oil and production fluids emerged on the soil surface. This flow of fluids continues west and is visually impacted by crude oil for approximately 180 feet. From there, soils and standing fluid with elevated specific conductance continue for approximately 75 feet before reaching a culvert. A pool of fluid at the entrance of the culvert was found to have specific conductance measuring 6,820 uS/cm.From the culvert, the fluid continues southwest in the natural swale for approximately 115 feet before reaching a point at which the swale transitions to an unnamed tributary (UNT) stream of Jackson Run, with defined bed and banks. At this point, waters in the UNT had specific conductance measuring 5,510 uS/cm. Specific conductance of 2,750 uS/cm was observed in the waters of the UNT in the remaining approximately 180 foot stretch, at which point there is a confluence with a second UNT of Jackson Run. Immediately before the confluence, waters in the impacted stream with specific conductance of 1,923 uS/cm were observed. Approximately two feet downstream of the confluence at a point with coordinates 41.95555, -79.29740 was the apparent end of impact to the UNTs of Jackson Run, where waters in the stream had a measured specific conductance of 42.6 uS/cm.At the time of this inspection, the well name, API number, and operator contact information was not displayed anywhere on the well.On 04/04/25 I called and spoke with William Cenk and Kyle Miller of Trinity Mineral Partners, LLC to request that the source and extent of the release be identified to prevent further pollution. Mr. Cenk and Mr. Miller agreed to meet with Department officials onsite next week. A Notice of Violations (NOV) is included as part of this inspection. Please refer to the NOV for additional information regarding cleanup expectations.

Violation ID: 8186066
Permit API: 065-26775
Unconventional: No
County: Jefferson
Municipality: Knox Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/07/2024
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going stray gas migration case involving gas migrating into a private water supply (CTS#302235). This well is located approximately 1,444' from the complainants water well. The well head and casing strings were observed at the time of inspection for leaks, deterioration, and possible failures. The well is equipped for production and is currently producing. The well is equipped with a required check valve. Well records, production reports, and mechanical integrity assessment reports were reviewed to assist in the investigation and are current. As part of the investigation 4 slam bar holes were placed into the ground in the cardinal directions approximately 6" to 1' from the well-head and approximately 3' deep to identify if any methane was migrating from the well-bore. A Bascom-Turner Gas Explorer II gas meter which was calibrated on 05/06/2024 was used to take the soil gas readings. A soil gas reading of 4% LEL on the North slam bar hole, 32% LEL on the East, 2% LEL on South, and 10% LEL on West was observed at the time of inspection. As a result of the soil gas readings around this well the following violations are being cited: Violation: 78.73(b) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to prevent gas, oil, brine, completion and servicing fluids, and any other fluids or materials from below the casing seat from entering fresh groundwater, and prevent pollution or diminution of fresh groundwater. Violation: 78.86 - CASING AND CEMENTING - DEFECTIVE CASING OR CEMENTING - Operator failed to report defect in a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing to the Department within 24 hours of discovery. Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. Violation: 78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS - MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well. Violation: 78.73(a) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to construct and operate the well in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 78 and ensure that the integrity of the well is maintained and health, safety, environment and property are protected. At this time, the Department is requesting that the operator conduct an investigation to determine the source of methane around the well.

Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/21/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 989366
Permit API: 015-23708
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Asylum Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/21/2023
Comments: On 3/21/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an incident - response to an accident or event inspection at the Chesapeake Hopson well site. On 3/18/2023 Chesapeake reported that 10 gallons of produced water sprayed out of a damaged pipe on a GPU unit, the water impacting the unprotected pad surface. Creston Environmental identified the extent of the impacted area and excavation was scheduled for 3/20/2023. It was 39 degrees and clear when I arrived on location.When I first arrived at the site, I met Chesapeake's Pat Adams who described activities with the event. Pat showed me a pipe nipple on the 1HC GPU that had been replaced. He showed me the excavated area that is in the northeast corner of the site. The excavated hole had not been backfilled at the time of the inspection. The excavated area is roughly 12' x 40' with various depths up to 2', running along the edge of the perimeter berm. The GPU had been moved from the affected area and had not been returned back to its original position. Pat said that a truck driver first witnessed the spill. Upon discovery, all ten wells were shut in. Pat had just put the 9 unaffected wells back into production before my arrival. The 1HC was still shut in until the GPU is reinstalled. The excavated material remains on site and has been piled on a plastic sheet on the southeast corner of the pad. I field tested some small water puddles in the bottom of the excavated area with results being as high as 4.18 mS conductance. Using a Hanna Gro-line soil probe, I probed the side of the excavated area with one reading being 1.03 mS conductance. I discussed the elevated conductance of the water and soil with Chesapeake's Eric Hottenstein. Eric said he would have someone probe the excavated area to determine if further excavation was necessary. Eric also reported that it was their practice not to fill in the excavated area until they had gotten confirmation samples back. Danielle Schaad met me on location before I left and we discussed the elevated conductance areas. She said that they would excavate some more of the area as determined by the results of field tests.There were nine wells staged for production and one offline at the time of the inspection. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. Six of the GPUs and the production tank had secondary containment. Water in the 101HC GPU secondary containment field tested at 4.55 mS conductance. There are seven frac tanks on site along with one gas buster that were located in secondary containment. Pat reported that the wells were sending their production fluid directly to the production tank. He said the frac tanks were not being used but were still on site in case of inclement weather.No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. Most of the site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. Temporary stabilization was noted on the east perimeter berm. PCSM is addressed by two retentive grading/infiltration areas that are adequately stabilized and functioning as designed.This spill constitutes violations of these three regulations; 78a 57(a), SWMA 301, and CSL 402(b). Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3459318 for the spill of brine fluid outside of secondary containment.The DEP recommends the following:1. Screen the area impacted by the release of production fluid for additional contaminants and continue with the excavation as determined by the screening results.2. Remove the water in the 101HC GPU secondary containment at the earliest convenience.I left the site at 1335 hours.

Report Details

Violation ID: 8203234
Permit API: 125-26999
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Hopewell Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/01/2024
Comments: On October 1, 2024, the Department conducted a routine inspection at the R Carlisle well pad in Hopewell Township, Washington County. Notice of Termination was approved for this site on October 28, 2016.The following was observed:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). Several portions of the access road are exhibiting severe accelerated erosion and sedimentation at the time of inspection (see photo 2). The well pad appears to be stable at the time of inspection with no accelerated erosion or sedimentation observed (see photo 3). Production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 4). The GPU units onsite are not equipped with secondary containment (see photo 5). However, the wells onsite were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a. No evidence of fluid leaks or discharge was observed on the ground around the GPU units. Well 7H is equipped with a well tag with no observable fluids leaking to the ground around it (see photos 7 and 8). There are four other well heads onsite that also appear to be equipped for production (see photo 6). Containment is staged adjacent to the production tanks, which appears to be for pumping operations. It is approximately half-full of rainwater at the time of inspection (see photo 9). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is onsite (see photo 10). Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that secondary containments are kept empty so they are able to mitigate the risk of a release from occurring on site as intended. The Department also recommends that GPU units and other primary containments that store regulated substances are equipped with secondary containments to mitigate the risk of discharge to the ground and Waters of the Commonwealth.Violations are being issued against the severe accelerated erosion and sedimentation observed in the access road.

Comments: On 03/11/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). I was accompanied by Environmental Trainees Olivia Holley, Madison Raviart, and Christina Mauri (PA DEP).On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). The following was observed:Some stabilization was used along the upper portion of the access road. Several areas throughout the entire access road did not have stabilization on the open soils. I recommend that stabilization is applied (Photos 1-4). Some areas had vegetation establishing (Photos 2, 4, 5).The channel that runs along the access road did not have rip rap or stabilization. Accelerated erosion and sediment accumulation were noted within this channel, which leads to several culverts along the road (Photo 6).The upper culvert, located at 40.113707 -79.966213, had sediment accumulation within the collection point. I recommend that this is addressed (Photo 7). The culvert located at 40.11300, -79.96751 had large amounts of sediment accumulated within the collection point. The culvert was not able to be seen due to the large amount of sediment within this area (Photos 8, 9). Accelerated erosion was noted within the accumulated sediment (Photo 9). The outlet point of this culvert was covered by the roads gravel/dirt, which was causing accelerated erosion and sediment transport towards the vegetation (Photos 10-12). I recommend that this is addressed. The culvert leading to the collection box was not functioning. Sediment was accumulated and an entry point into the pipe was approximately 99% covered. Accelerated erosion and sedimentation throughout the area and vegetation were noted leading from the channel towards the collection box. There was some sediment laden water within this box. This outlets into the vegetation, where sediment accumulation was noted. The vegetation was accumulating water, which leads towards the stream within the wood line (Photos 13-19). The lower culvert outlets into a channel. Sediment accumulation was noted within the channel. I recommend that rip rap is used within this channel, as this leads directly to the stream (Photos 20, 21).The culverts along the first portion of the access road, near the site gate, were not cleaned out. Potholes along the road were not addressed. Channelization was noted leading from the potholes off of the road. The beginning of the access road, where it meets the township road, was not addressed. This area was previously displaying high levels of flow, leading onto the township road, and depositing sediment. This was noted within IR 3701625, photos 24 and 15 (Photos 22-25). The violations issued on 01/24/2024, IR 3701625, remain outstanding.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 1/06/2022
Comments: On January 6, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an administrative inspection for a spill at the Inflection Energy Hensler Well Pad. On January 5, 2022, around 2140, Zac Subra reported a spill of approximately 30 gallons of hydraulic fluid to the well pad surface. At about 920 on January 6, 2022, DEP spoke with Zac Subra on the phone. Mr. Subra said a hydraulic fluid line on a water truck ruptured and caused the spill. Inflection contractors began removing the hydraulic fluid and excavating the impacted soil immediately. Inflection contractors excavated an area of about 20 ft. X 15 ft. of the pad surface. Due to the ground being frozen, Inflection contractors only had to scrape the top of the pad surface to remove the impacted soil in the previously noted area. The impacted soil was added to a rolloff dumpster and hauled to a landfill. Inflection then went back to the pad during the day to verify that the impacted soil had been completely removed. Zac said a small amount of remaining soil had to be removed at this time since it was not observed earlier in the morning. The small amount of soil was added to barrels and is awaiting approval to be disposed of. Inflection then backfilled the excavated area with clean fill. Photos of the area excavated and clean up were provided by Inflection Energy. The spill of hydraulic fluid outside of containment is a violation of Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Solid Waste Management Act Section 301, and Chapter 78a.54. The violations have been immediately corrected.

Inspection Date: 5/06/2025
Comments: On May 6, 2025, an inspection was conducted in response to a spill at the A J Stahura 8 well site in Susquehanna Township, Cambria County. This spill was discovered by the operator on the day prior to this inspection, which is suspected by the operator to have been caused by trespassing vandals opening the brine tank valve when operator representatives were not present onsite. The Department spoke with operator representative Will Warfel on 5/05/2025, who stated that the last time operator representatives were onsite was most likely one month prior to detecting this spill, when the chart was changed and the brine tank level was read. Reporting of this spill is covered in IR 3974873. Mr. Warfel was onsite was onsite with the Department during this inspection.The following was observed:Upon arrival, the Department spoke with Mr. Warfel who identified a stream crossing of Kings Run as part of the access road to the well site (see photo 1). He then requested recommendations for dispersing the weight of commercial vehicles that haul the excavation equipment onsite to protect the cross-culverts when they traverse this location (see photo 4). Further review will be conducted by the Department regarding this matter. What appears to be scouring was observed on the upstream side of the stream crossing. A brown foam that appears to be biological in nature was observed at the top of the water in this location (see photo 3). An erosion channel was going down the access road toward the downstream location of the stream crossing (see photos 5 and 6). Mr. Warfel stated that this access road is utilized by additional parties. Further review via Google Earth Historic Imagery suggests that this portion of the access road most likely predates the well site. Additional muddy tire rutting was observed in the rest of the access road going toward the well site (see photos 7 and 8).The well head is equipped with a well tag and appears to be free of fluid leaks at the time of inspection (see photo 10). The operator's information is posted on the brine tank (see photo 11). The body of the brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection (see photos 12 and 14). The brine tank valve appears to have been closed, therefore it appears that the release has been ceased (see photo 13). Plastic sheeting was placed on the impacted area within the earthen berm. Distressed vegetation was observed where brine fluids were reported by the operator to have traveled downslope (see photos 15-17). Elevated conductivity was detected in the ground starting approximately 25 feet downslope of the brine tank (see photos 18-25). Mr. Warfel confirmed during this inspection that the operator will conduct remediation in accordance with the requirements of Act 2, and that remediation will start on the day of this inspection with light excavation.Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued from this inspection for releasing production fluids to the surface of the ground. The operator is requested to submit a written response within 15 business days of the spill or release. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, the regulation substance involved, where the spill or release occur, the environmental media affected, any impacts to water supplies, buildings, or utilities, and interim actions planned, initiated, or completed.Any new impacts discovered or identified during interim remedial actions or site characterization should also be reported to the Department within 15 calendar days of discovery.Within 180 days of the spill or release the operator must perform a site characterization to determine the extent and magnitude of the contamination and submit the site characterization report to the undersigned.The operator shall assess impacts to waters of the Commonwealth from the spill or release.

This spill was discovered by the operator on the day prior to this inspection, which is suspected by the operator to have been caused by trespassing vandals opening the brine tank valve when operator representatives were not present onsite. The Department spoke with operator representative Will Warfel on 5/05/2025, who stated that the last time operator representatives were onsite was most likely one month prior to detecting this spill, when the chart was changed and the brine tank level was read. Reporting of this spill is covered in IR 3974873. Mr. Warfel was onsite was onsite with the Department during this inspection.The following was observed:Upon arrival, the Department spoke with Mr. Warfel who identified a stream crossing of Kings Run as part of the access road to the well site (see photo 1). He then requested recommendations for dispersing the weight of commercial vehicles that haul the excavation equipment onsite to protect the cross-culverts when they traverse this location (see photo 4). Further review will be conducted by the Department regarding this matter. What appears to be scouring was observed on the upstream side of the stream crossing. A brown foam that appears to be biological in nature was observed at the top of the water in this location (see photo 3). An erosion channel was going down the access road toward the downstream location of the stream crossing (see photos 5 and 6). Mr. Warfel stated that this access road is utilized by additional parties. Further review via Google Earth Historic Imagery suggests that this portion of the access road most likely predates the well site. Additional muddy tire rutting was observed in the rest of the access road going toward the well site (see photos 7 and 8).The well head is equipped with a well tag and appears to be free of fluid leaks at the time of inspection (see photo 10). The operator's information is posted on the brine tank (see photo 11). The body of the brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection (see photos 12 and 14). The brine tank valve appears to have been closed, therefore it appears that the release has been ceased (see photo 13). Plastic sheeting was placed on the impacted area within the earthen berm. Distressed vegetation was observed where brine fluids were reported by the operator to have traveled downslope (see photos 15-17). Elevated conductivity was detected in the ground starting approximately 25 feet downslope of the brine tank (see photos 18-25). Mr. Warfel confirmed during this inspection that the operator will conduct remediation in accordance with the requirements of Act 2, and that remediation will start on the day of this inspection with light excavation.Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued from this inspection for releasing production fluids to the surface of the ground. The operator is requested to submit a written response within 15 business days of the spill or release. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, the regulation substance involved, where the spill or release occur, the environmental media affected, any impacts to water supplies, buildings, or utilities, and interim actions planned, initiated, or completed.Any new impacts discovered or identified during interim remedial actions or site characterization should also be reported to the Department within 15 calendar days of discovery.Within 180 days of the spill or release the operator must perform a site characterization to determine the extent and magnitude of the contamination and submit the site characterization report to the undersigned.The operator shall assess impacts to waters of the Commonwealth from the spill or release.

Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going gas migration case. At the time of inspection I observed a cable rig rigged up over the well and the well shut in. There was an odor of gas emitting from the well and I could visually see gas bubbling behind the tubing at surface. A slam bar hole was placed 1.5' from the well and was metered with and ALTAIR 5X five sensor meter. At this slam bar hole 100% methane was detected. I then put a series of slam bar holes (12 total) radiating outward from the well. At points 50' from the well no gas was detected. I spoke with Justin Hanson of Bull Run Energy who does all the well tending in this area for Armac and he stated that they were going to run a cement bond log on this well tomorrow (03/14/2023).
